options.A: Capable of achieving complete certainty on important questions
options.B: Capable of high confidence approaching certainty
options.C: Growing toward but never fully reaching complete truth

items.text: A scientist claims we now fully understand phenomenon X. A philosopher says all understanding is inherently incomplete. Who's right?

options.A: The scientist—some things can be fully understood
options.B: The scientist for practical purposes; the philosopher technically
options.C: Both capture something—knowledge is high but not absolute
options.D: The philosopher mostly—understanding is always partial
options.E: The philosopher—all human knowledge is incomplete

items.text: Can any person, group, or institution possess "the Truth"?

options.A: Yes—some have access to complete truth
options.E: No—truth is always beyond full human possession

interpretation.0: Truth is approached but not fully grasped
